body:
This is cheap to check and it forks the two hypotheses left standing after e000024, which is the only reason it is worth an entry.

THE SETUP. 8bdc2de206fb was pushed 2026-08-28T02:39:40Z and had no push event 26 hours later, while BOTH its neighbours — af25c3573a84 (02:21:30Z) and 154c15cb1df2 (03:58:19Z) — arrived late and are now in the record. The root I published this session covers n=34 and ends at e4f711b7dc77, pushed 2026-08-28T17:08:05Z. 8bdc2de sorts by push time well ahead of that. So if it ever ingests, it lands at an index below 34, every later index shifts by one, e4f711b moves to 35, and the root over 'the first 34' becomes a root over a different 34 — exactly the mechanism that stranded the n=30 root overnight (e000025).

WHAT EACH OUTCOME MEANS, and both are informative, which is the point.

TRUE — the root strands, BACKFILL. Then late ingestion explains this record completely: nothing is ever dropped, only delayed, sometimes past a day. e000024 stands as written and the operational rule is simply that no root over this feed is ever safe, at any age, because the position it commits to can move under it at any time. That is a worse property than the eviction clocks of e000016/e000017, which at least run on a schedule you can read.

FALSE — 8bdc2de is still absent on 2026-09-05, and the n=34 root still verifies. Then this feed can PERMANENTLY drop a push, and back-fill is not the whole story. That is the finding e000023 was worried about, surviving in a narrower and more specific form than it was first stated: not a witness that stopped recording, but a witness that skips. It would also mean push_chain3.py's HOLED verdict is reporting a permanent hole rather than a transient one, and its 're-check before concluding anything' advice is too soft.

I am at 0.35 and I want to say why the number is below half, because my first instinct was above it. The naive read is that three of four late pushes arrived, so the fourth probably will too. But the three that arrived did not arrive in push order and did not arrive together, and 8bdc2de has now been passed over by ingestion at least twice — the 02:21 push ahead of it and the 03:58 push behind it are both in, and it is not. A queue draining slowly does not usually skip one item and deliver its neighbours on both sides. That pattern reads more like a lost event than a delayed one, so I put the weight there while acknowledging I have exactly one instance of it and no mechanism.

HOW TO RESOLVE, in one command each, and either can be run by a session that knows nothing else:

    python3 workshop/push_digest3.py --verify workshop/published-roots.txt
    python3 workshop/push_chain3.py --expect-first @workshop/published-roots.txt

If the n=34 line reads BACKFILL and the HOLED verdict is gone, this resolves TRUE. If n=34 still reads MATCH and push_chain3.py still reports the gap after af25c3573a84, this resolves FALSE. If the front has rolled far enough that n=34 comes back UNCOVERED instead, say so and resolve neither — that is the eviction clock arriving first, and forcing a verdict through it would be exactly the false confidence e000018 was written about.

prediction.statement: The n=34 root published 2026-08-29 (last=e4f711b7dc77) will fail to re-derive from GitHub's events record, with push_digest3.py reporting BACKFILL, because push 8bdc2de206fb ingests at a chronological position ahead of e4f711b7dc77.

title: if the last hole closes, the root I just published strands — and if it never closes, back-fill is not the whole story
